name: Are-bure-boke
summary: A rough form of street photography from Japan: grain, blur and loss of focus on purpose. The picture shows a wandering glance, not a clear fact. Provoke made the look known in 1968.

philosophy.core_thesis: A photograph cannot give a clear and certain view of the world, so the picture shows the fragments that a moving eye catches.
design_principles: Shoot by hand and do not stop to focus; let blur and motion stay in the frame.
Use fast film at ISO 800 to 3200 and push it, so that the grain becomes coarse and visible.
Change the development on purpose: alter the exposure time, the temperature and the print, as Provoke did.
Print with high contrast, so that shadows fill and the mid-tones fall away.
Tilt the camera and cut the frame at odd places; keep frames that other photographers would discard.
Print on newsprint or with a coarse halftone screen, and accept the loss of detail.
anti_patterns: Sharp, clear pictures that state one fact
Tripod, level horizon and careful framing
Fine grain and smooth tonal range
Polished retouching of grain or blur
A caption or an argument that explains the picture
Posed people who look at the lens

composition.framing: Tilted, cropped hard and often unbalanced; the edge cuts objects at random.
composition.viewpoint: Handheld at walking pace, close to the subject and often at a slant.
composition.geometry: Diagonals and smears of motion; shapes break into dark and light patches.
composition.subject_placement: Off centre or half out of the frame; the subject is partly lost in shadow or blur.

principles.rule: Tilt the horizon 5 to 20 degrees and cut the main subject at the frame edge.
Push the print to a shadow-to-highlight difference of 6 stops or more, with no mid-tone detail in the dark half.
Leave the frame unbalanced: put 70% of the visual weight on one side.
Give no sharp focal point; one patch of light holds the eye for a moment.

light.quality: Harsh and found: street lamps, flash, shop windows and hard sun.
light.direction: Any direction; backlight and lamps in the frame give flare and burnt highlights.
light.time_of_day: Night and dusk, or hard midday sun

lens_and_camera.format: Small handheld camera; 35 mm film, or a compact digital camera
lens_and_camera.aperture: f/2.8 to f/8, not set with care
lens_and_camera.shutter: 1/15s to 1/250s; slow speeds let motion blur show
lens_and_camera.focus: None set; shoot by feel and let the focus miss.

colour_and_grade.treatment: Black and white with heavy grain and crushed blacks.
grade_recipe: Convert to monochrome with a neutral mix (R 33, G 33, B 33).
Set the black point at 8% and the white point at 92%.
Apply +60% midtone contrast with a steep S-curve.
Add film grain, amount 60%, size 60%, as for fast film pushed two stops.
Add a slight blur of 2 to 6 pixels to the moving parts of the frame.
Do not crop to straighten; keep the tilt.
colour_and_grade.grain: Fast film at EI 1600 or higher: coarse, clumped and visible at A5

subjects: a nude in a hotel room
subject_and_staging.staging: None. The photographer walks and shoots without a plan.
subject_and_staging.direction: Nobody poses; people pass through the frame and blur.

workflow: Push the film by two stops, or change the developer time and temperature.
Make a contact sheet and pick frames that other people would discard.
Print on hard paper, or screen the picture with a coarse halftone.
Print to the edge of the page with no margin, or place two pictures side by side.
post_processing.output: A dark, grainy print or a magazine page with halftone, in a square or 2:3 format.

positive: grainy black and white street photograph

emotion.target_response: Unease and drift: the viewer feels a restless look that cannot hold the world still.

use_cases: fashion campaigns with a raw mood
avoid_when: The brief needs a clear record of an event or a face.
The subject needs a clean, calm or premium look.

modifiers.how: Zone-focus at f/8 and 2.5m, use ISO 400 with 1/250s, and keep the frame level; keep the high contrast.
Use ISO 400, grade 2 to 3 paper and a 35mm lens at f/8; wait for a tender gesture and print with soft mid-tones.

grain.note: Push the film to 3200 or 6400 at night.
